declaration.preface:
This Ethics Policy sets out the binding ethical principles and compliance obligations of Prestige Promotion Verkaufsförderung & Werbeservice GmbH ("Prestige Promotion"). It defines qualitative commitments, detailed measures, and quantitative objectives.

The policy is based on the principles of the honourable merchant, the UN Global Compact, the German Criminal Code (StGB), the German Money Laundering Act (GwG), the German Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG), the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and applicable international anti-corruption standards including the UK Bribery Act 2010 and the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA).
declaration.declaration:
Prestige Promotion follows the principle of the honourable merchant and acknowledges its responsibility as a company operating in the highly regulated pharmaceutical co-packaging sector.

Prestige Promotion supports the ten principles of the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) covering human rights, labour, environment and anti-corruption, and commits to integrating these into its corporate governance. The company is actively reviewing formal accession to the UNGC.
declaration.scope:
This policy applies without exception to:

All employees of Prestige Promotion: full-time, part-time, fixed-term, casual workers, interns and apprentices

Management and all members of the leadership team, regardless of position

Temporary workers, external consultants and contractors acting on behalf of the company

Business partners, suppliers and service providers, to the extent contractually agreed

All business activities and sites of Prestige Promotion, worldwide and regardless of whether local laws impose less stringent requirements

Corruption: Prestige Promotion maintains an unconditional zero-tolerance towards all forms of corruption and bribery. This applies to all business activities, both domestic and international, regardless of local customs or market conditions. No financial or commercial interest justifies deviation from this commitment. Management exercises a role-model function and bears personal responsibility for creating an environment in which corruption cannot arise.

The following conduct is prohibited without exception: Offering, promising, granting or approving advantages to public officials or business partners in exchange for preferential treatment in decisions, contract awards or supply arrangements.
Demanding, accepting a promise of, or receiving personal advantages in exchange for preferential treatment in a supply arrangement or contract award is prohibited.
Facilitation payments of any kind, including to public officials, are prohibited.
Kickback payments, covert commissions or payments to intermediaries where it is known or reasonably assumed that these will be used for bribery are prohibited.
Participation in bid-rigging arrangements or anti-competitive agreements with competitors is prohibited.
Covert payments via third parties (consultants, asset managers, agents) intended to circumvent anti-corruption controls are prohibited.
Any conduct creating the appearance of attempting to influence business or governmental decisions through improper means is prohibited.
Prestige Promotion conducts a formal corruption risk assessment at least once per year.

The assessment covers identification of company areas exposed to corruption risk, assessment of the likelihood of occurrence and extent of damage, determination and documentation of appropriate anti-corruption control measures, derivation and approval of a corrective and preventive action plan (CAPA plan), and submission to and approval by management as part of the annual management review (QMH Chapter 5.7).

All gifts and entertainment above threshold limits are recorded in the Gifts & Entertainment Register and evaluated annually. Gifts or entertainment during ongoing contract negotiations or tendering processes are prohibited.
Priority Actions 2026: Conduct first annual corruption risk assessment | Launch gifts & entertainment register | Anti-corruption training for purchasing & sales
Conflict of Interest: Prestige Promotion requires all employees to act in the best interest of the company at all times and to avoid situations in which personal interests conflict or could conflict with the objective fulfilment of their professional duties. All potential or actual conflicts of interest must be disclosed without delay. The company ensures that reported conflicts are assessed, managed and documented transparently and impartially.

Examples include business relationships with family members or close friends where the employee has influence over a relevant decision; secondary employment or consultancy activities for competitors, customers, or suppliers without prior disclosure and approval; direct or indirect shareholdings in current or prospective business partners; receipt of personal benefits in connection with supplier selection, contract award or procurement decisions; participation in a hiring or performance evaluation decision involving a personal relationship; and use of confidential information for personal financial gain or for the benefit of third parties.

All employees are required to report potential or actual conflicts of interest to their line manager and/or the compliance function without delay, and before acting in any matter where a conflict may exist.

Employees in key positions — including purchasing, management, project management and senior quality roles — sign a formal annual conflict of interest declaration confirming disclosure of all known or potential conflicts.
The compliance function and management assess each reported conflict, determine appropriate management measures (recusal, oversight, transfer of responsibility), and document the outcome.
Employees are not disadvantaged for making good-faith disclosures; retaliation against employees who disclose conflicts is prohibited and will be treated as a disciplinary matter.
Line managers are trained to recognise indicators of undisclosed conflicts of interest and to manage disclosures with confidentiality and impartiality.
Priority Actions 2026: Launch annual conflict of interest declaration for key functions | Establish documentation register | Deliver targeted training for purchasing, management & project leads
Fraud: Prestige Promotion maintains zero tolerance towards all forms of fraud, embezzlement, falsification of documents, manipulation of accounts, theft or deception — whether committed by employees, contractors or business partners. The company implements a robust system of preventive controls, detection mechanisms and response procedures to ensure that fraud risks are systematically identified and addressed.

The following conduct is prohibited: falsification of documents, reports, invoices, contracts, test records, quality documentation, or any other business record; manipulation of accounts, financial reports, inventory records or any system-generated data; embezzlement, misappropriation or unauthorised use of company assets, funds or property; submission of false expense claims or claims for work not performed; deception of customers, suppliers, authorities or other stakeholders; theft or misappropriation of physical assets, intellectual property or confidential information; circumvention of internal controls, approval processes or segregation of duty requirements; and collusion with external parties to defraud the company or any third party.

The four-eyes principle is applied to all payment approvals, contract awards, purchase orders above defined thresholds, and significant financial transactions — two independent approvals are required before execution.
A defined and documented authorisation matrix specifies approval authority limits by role and transaction type and is regularly reviewed and updated as part of the management review process.
Incompatible functions are segregated: the person who initiates a transaction may not be the same person who approves and processes payment.
Regular internal audits and self-inspections are conducted in accordance with SOP-16.01, including unannounced spot checks of financial records, expense claims, inventory and document integrity.

Data integrity controls in accordance with SOP-10.03 and SOP-10.04 ensure that all quality-relevant and financial records are complete, accurate, traceable, contemporaneous, original and attributable (ALCOA+).
GMP-compliant batch record and documentation controls prevent unauthorised modification of pharmaceutical packaging records, serialisation data and quality system entries.
Fraud awareness and prevention training is provided for functions at elevated risk, including accounting, purchasing, logistics and warehouse management.

Priority Actions 2026: Formalise and communicate authorisation matrix | Expand internal audit plan to cover fraud-risk processes | Launch fraud awareness training for accounting & logistics | Quarterly expense claim spot checks
Money Laundering: Prestige Promotion is committed to preventing any involvement — direct or indirect — in money laundering, the concealment of unlawfully obtained funds, or the financing of criminal or terrorist activities. The company will not enter into, maintain or facilitate business relationships that serve to disguise the origin, ownership or disposition of illicit funds. All business transactions are conducted transparently, lawfully and with full accountability.

The following conduct is prohibited: accepting, processing or transferring funds where there are reasonable grounds to suspect unlawful origin; structuring transactions to avoid reporting obligations or regulatory scrutiny; establishing or maintaining fictitious accounts, black funds or covert financial arrangements; accepting unusual cash payments without adequate justification and documentation; entering into relationships with parties known to be associated with criminal activities or subject to financial sanctions; and issuing or accepting fictitious invoices, false invoice descriptions or payments without a legitimate commercial basis.

Prior to entering into significant new business relationships, Prestige Promotion verifies the identity, business purpose and beneficial ownership of counterparties, with particular attention to politically exposed persons (PEPs), sanctioned parties and high-risk jurisdictions.
All new and existing significant business partners are screened against applicable EU, UN, OFAC and national sanctions lists; screening is documented and repeated on a risk-based basis.

Employees are trained to identify and report red flags including payments to or from unknown third parties, requests for unusual payment routes, unusually large or split cash transactions, and payments without apparent commercial justification.
All payments are made only to verified counterparties on the basis of proper documentation; payments to third parties on behalf of a business partner require additional approval and justification.

All business transactions are completely, truthfully and promptly recorded; no fictitious entries or transactions without economic substance are permitted; the four-eyes principle applies to all payment-relevant transactions.

Employees who detect or reasonably suspect money laundering activity are required to report immediately to management and/or the compliance function; statutory reporting obligations to competent authorities are fulfilled where required by law.
Priority Actions 2026: Define and implement KYC procedure for new significant business partners | Establish sanctions screening process | Cash payment policy documentation
Responsible Information Management: Prestige Promotion is committed to the responsible, lawful and ethical management of all information in its care — including personal data of employees, customers, business partners and patients; confidential business information; intellectual property; and GMP-relevant quality records. The company respects the privacy rights of all individuals, protects confidential information entrusted to it, maintains data integrity across all systems, and responds promptly and transparently to data protection incidents.

Unauthorised access, sharing of passwords or access rights, unlawful or unauthorised disclosure or misuse of personal data, disclosure of confidential information, unauthorised use of personal devices or software, falsification or destruction of records, circumvention of cybersecurity controls, unauthorised software, and use of company information systems for unlawful, fraudulent, discriminatory, harassing, or otherwise unethical purposes are strictly prohibited.

All personal data is processed strictly in accordance with the GDPR, the BDSG and internal data protection policies. Personal data is collected only for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes; data minimisation is applied.
All employees with access to personal data receive mandatory GDPR awareness training upon induction and annually thereafter; training is documented in the training management system.
Data subjects' rights — including access, rectification, erasure, portability and objection — are respected and can be exercised through documented procedures.
Personal data is shared with third parties only where a lawful basis exists; data processing agreements are in place with all relevant third-party processors.
Internal company data is classified and protected in accordance with SOP-03.03, with access granted strictly on a need-to-know basis.

Confidential information belonging to customers, business partners and suppliers is treated with the same level of protection as internal confidential data; non-disclosure obligations are contractually documented.
Intellectual property of Prestige Promotion and of business partners and customers is respected; unauthorised reproduction, disclosure or use is prohibited.
Employees leaving the company are required to return all company devices, data and confidential materials; access rights are revoked promptly upon termination.
All GMP-relevant records comply with ALCOA+ principles: Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate, plus Complete, Consistent, Enduring and Available.
Unauthorised modification, deletion or falsification of GMP records is treated as a critical compliance violation subject to immediate escalation, root cause investigation and CAPA.
Audit trails in electronic systems used for quality-critical processes are activated, protected and reviewed as required by EU GMP Annex 11.

Internal IT systems and data repositories are protected through role-based access controls, password policies, and appropriate technical and organisational security measures proportionate to the risk of the data held.

In the event of a personal data breach, the internal escalation procedure is immediately initiated; reportable breaches are notified to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours in accordance with GDPR Article 33, and to affected individuals where required.
A mandatory reporting obligation applies to all employees who become aware of an actual or suspected data breach, data loss, or unauthorised access to company systems or confidential information.
Priority Actions 2026: Complete register of data processors and DPA review | Formalise data breach response procedure | Annual GDPR refresher training | IT access revocation process for leavers

policy.monitoring:
The management of Prestige Promotion commits to conducting an annual corruption risk assessment and integrating the results into the annual management review.

The management of Prestige Promotion commits to maintaining effective whistleblower and reporting mechanisms in compliance with the German Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG).

The management of Prestige Promotion commits to ensuring regular communication of ethical obligations to all employees and relevant stakeholders.

Prestige Promotion has established an internal reporting office in compliance with the German Whistleblower Protection Act (HinSchG) and the underlying EU Whistleblower Protection Directive.

All employees, external partners and other parties may report indications of possible violations of this policy, applicable law or ethical standards — regardless of employment status, nationality or position.

Non-retaliation: whistleblowers who make reports in good faith will not be disadvantaged, dismissed, transferred, demoted or otherwise adversely treated; any retaliation constitutes a violation of this policy and the HinSchG.

Confidentiality: the identity of the whistleblower is protected in strict confidence; anonymous reports are accepted and processed equally.

Impartiality: the reporting office acts independently; it does not report to the person or function against whom a complaint is made.

Feedback: acknowledgement of receipt provided within 7 days; feedback on follow-up measures within 3 months from acknowledgement.

Documentation: all reports are documented and retained for a minimum of 3 years, or longer if required by applicable law or ongoing proceedings.

The reporting procedure, contact information and protection guarantees are provided in at least German and English to ensure accessible reporting for all employees regardless of language background.

Compliance with this policy is mandatory for all employees. Prestige Promotion ensures that all persons covered by this policy have the knowledge and awareness necessary to fulfil their obligations.
policy.reviewMechanism:
The management of Prestige Promotion commits to reviewing and updating this policy at least annually, incorporating changes in law, and operational experience.

The management of Prestige Promotion commits to applying appropriate sanctions — including employment law and criminal law consequences — to any violations of this policy.

Annual Policy Review: Review for currency and compliance with changes in law (StGB, GwG, HinSchG, GDPR). Frequency: Annually (Q1).

Corruption Risk Assessment: Formal annual assessment covering all risk areas; CAPA plan approved by management. Frequency: Annually (Q2).

Management Review: Integration of ethics and compliance KPIs into annual QM management review. Frequency: Annually (Q4).

KPI Monitoring: Semi-annual review of quantitative targets by QMO / Compliance. Frequency: Semi-annually.

Gifts & Entertainment Register Review: Annual review of all entries; verification of compliance with thresholds and approvals. Frequency: Annually (Q4).

Event-driven Revision: In the event of incidents, complaints, new legislation, or supply chain findings. Frequency: As required (ad hoc).

The following priority measures are to be implemented to fulfil all applicable legal obligations.
